text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Iran expresses readiness to sign defence pacts with Gulf Arab states. Since the 1979 Islamic revolution in Tehran ties between non-Arab Iran and its six pro-Western Gulf neighbours have often been tense.
- Iranian embassy criticises al-Rai al-Aam daily for publshing an interview earlier this month with the son of the late Shah of Iran Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.
- Some 20 billion shares worth 5.7 billion dinars ($18.87 billion) were traded on the Kuwait Stock Exchange in the first six months of 1997.
- Some 15 companies were set up under the Saudi Arabian offset programme. Defence Minister Prince Sultan says more than $746 million are invested in the kingdom under the programme.
- Interior Minister Sheikh Mohammad Khaled al-Sabah flies to Bahrain on official visit.
- Hong Kong visa procedures unchanged for Kuwaitis.
- Liberal parliamentarian Sami al-Munayes plans to question Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan.
- MP submits draft law to ban human cloning.
- France decorates Kuwaiti journalist Nawaf Naman.
